notes:
The Uptown Tenderloin Historic District nomination (08001407, listed 5 February 2009), read for the theatre addresses named in issue #302 and for nothing else. Its section 7 inventory runs to roughly four hundred properties across thirty-three blocks and is unread; that pass is a batch of its own and is filed as issue #304, not attempted here.

One of the fifteen theatre parcels in #302 falls inside the district: 76-80 Turk Street, which the inventory records as the Gaiety Theater. The other fourteen are outside the boundary, and the nomination's own Theaters section says why the district holds so few — the post-fire theatres rebuilt on Market Street and in the adjacent Market Street Theater and Loft district, and only a handful ever stood inside these thirty-three blocks.

The reference number is the trap in this batch. The Uptown Tenderloin is 08001407; 08000209, which is what a plausible guess at an early-2008 San Francisco listing produces, serves a nomination for Johnston's Inn in Paris, Kentucky, with San Francisco nowhere in it. The NPS index is the only way to a reference number.

  The section 7 inventory was read in full on 2026-09-11 under issue #304. It is a per-property table in a regular grammar -- historic and later names, use, construction year, owner, architect, storeys, structure, facade, composition, ornamentation, signs and dated alterations, semicolon-delimited -- which makes it the densest single document in this source: 446 findings from 477 rows, 308 of them naming an architect.

  Two things in that grammar decide whether an entry is true. A name in parentheses is a LATER name and the year is when that name was current, not when the building went up: 71 rows lead with a dated name, and asserting 'built as' it would be false -- 134-144 Eddy Street is dated 1907 and its first name is 'Langham Hotel (1911)'. And a dated event is often stated inside another clause rather than in the date slot: 25 rows carry one, including the theatre converted to a garage in 1929 at 35-65 Mason Street that issue #304 named.

  Every ownership clause was dropped at extraction time. 420 of the 477 rows name an owner, several give a trade and an ownership role in one clause ('architect and owner Smith and Stewart', 'builder and owner E.V. Lacey'), and those keep the trade credit and lose the role.

  No person is published out of this document, and one group was left on the table deliberately. Twelve rows append free prose after the structured fields naming a notable past resident with dates -- Dashiell Hammett at 620 Eddy Street when he began writing, Frank Capra at 233-237 Eddy in 1921, Fritz Leiber at 807-815 Geary 1969-1977, Miriam Allen de Ford at 35-65 Mason 1936-1975, Sally Stanford at 791-793 O'Farrell in 1931, and Jessie Hayman and Tessie Wall, whom the nomination cites to Gentry 1964. All are dead, documented and already in published sources, which is the case root AGENTS.md's notable_residents carve-out is written for; the research rulebook's 'leave residents and occupants' and issue #304's own instruction both point the other way. Publishing seven residents on that ambiguity is a presentation decision for a person, so this run took none of them and none reached a findings entry. That prose is also why the extractor cuts an alterations clause at its first sentence boundary: the tail is where the people are.

coverage.remaining: Nothing of 08001407 remains: the section 7 inventory has now been read in full, all 477 rows across 33 blocks, together with the one row (76-80 Turk Street) read earlier under #302. Still unread in this source: the five district nominations of 1982-1989 (82000983 Bush Street-Cottage Row, 83001230 Liberty Street, 87002286 Russian Hill-Macondray Lane, 87002288 Russian Hill-Paris Block, 87002289 Russian Hill-Vallejo Street Crest) and 89000319 Southern Pacific Company Hospital, all fetched and extracted; the 68 listings certified 1990 or later; and 77000334, 01000281 and 100008228, whose PDFs carry no text layer or serve a placeholder.
coverage.note: 477 inventory rows read, one per property. 480 findings were written from 445 of those rows -- one construction entry each, plus 35 dated later events (an addition, a rebuilding, or a conversion the row states inside another clause). 37 rows produced none: 24 carry no building (parking lots, vacant lots and sites under construction in 2007), 7 state no construction date the site can place, 5 are unreadable in the OCR (the Adelaide Place row lost its street number entirely, 'Ill Jones Street' lost its, and two Shannon rows are a parking lot and a vacant lot), and 1 is the 76-80 Turk row already held as 0001/0002. Of the 445 rows that yielded a finding, 408 carry a block and lot the OCR left clean, 27 carry one it damaged and 10 print none at all; the damaged values are kept verbatim under block_lot_as_printed and deliberately withheld from the resolver, because an inventory row's block and lot is judged against its neighbours rather than repaired in isolation.

findings.description: Built as the Gaiety Theater, a conversion of stores and a loft to a theatre, to the design of the architect Earl B. Bertz. Two storeys, reinforced concrete with a stucco facade and cast ornament, pilasters and pointed arches at the second level, Gothic ornamentation on a two-part commercial block composition, with a horizontal blade sign.
